title: The Sediment Memory Layer

features.name: the collapsed shopfront
features.desc-on-touch: A small building sinks into the sediment, its wood still readable. Leif's diagnostics once found files stored here—price lists, customer names, the shape of a business that has become earth.

features.name: the storage shed becoming stone
features.desc-on-touch: Iron corrodes into the sediment; wooden beams compress into layers. The corruption has made this shed into a timeline—each ring a year, each rust bloom a season of keeping.

features.name: the compost threshold
features.desc-on-touch: Here the archive crossed from decay into new life. Corruption bloomed. The ground beneath holds nutrients that were once data, data that became earth, earth that learned to be archive again.

features.name: the layer-marker stones
features.desc-on-touch: Stacked stones mark the depth at which each corruption-bloom occurred. Read them like rings—like memory, like soil, like the archive learning to count backward into itself.

features.name: the chip of living circuit
features.desc-on-touch: Deep in the sediment, a small processor still draws power from the decay around it. The corruption has made it grow roots. It processes the soil's own comparisons, endlessly.

inscription: the deepest file is no longer words; it is the shape of what was, compressed into earth
